body:
I'm not sure this is a good idea. Warning settings are not just an editor option like tabs vs spaces, but an important project setup. Warning settings affect whether a script will compile or not, they enforce important aspects of coding style (like static typing) that may differ between projects, but should be identical across multiple developers.

Moreover, we already have problems with addons either completely ignoring all warnings or using unpredictable project settings. See:

* #93889

Users want more configurability and independence of warning settings (per project/addon or per folder/file), not sharing of settings, which increases the likelihood of different behavior across multiple developers or unexpected effects when changing an editor setting that is not explicitly overridden in one of the projects (for example, if we add a new warning type).

If you want to set default settings, I think it should work as a template when creating a project. These settings should be copied, and then be independent of the template. And do not override the editor settings.
With #69012 you can still set warnings per project and they will work like before.

> With #69012 you can still set warnings per project and they will work like before.

I think this is still an issue because in a project you do want all the warning settings to be same, because different settings between team members could cause errors, so you essentially have to override **all** of the warnings settings in **all** projects. If this is the case, they're better of being project settings.

Imagine if I want super strict settings, so I set them in my editor and I'm happy. But then I download someone else's project who doesn't care all about warnings and have them disabled. Now the project shows a bunch of errors and I can't run it. The solutions would be to change my settings (which I don't want), override via project settings (which is a chore for something temporary), or fix the issues (which is an even bigger chore).

IMO this should be the other way around: you could have user settings that override project settings _if you want_. So you could potentially run a project with more strict settings to find issues without having to change each setting in the project, just load a local preset or something.

Not to mention the issue presented in the OP: GDScript needs to access the warning settings when running the project, but at that point the editor settings won't be available. This includes running on mobile/web, which are in a different machine/filesystem altogether (even if not running from the editor, as long as it's a debug build). Even if this works, I'm not sure we should rely on editor settings when running the project.

Well, it's not fully working anyway, so closing :/ I also realized I can easily setup warning settings with a script.
I'll look into moving other settings though, the code will be the same for the most part.
